modal.$description: Centered modal dialog — native <dialog> with showModal(): free focus-trap, Escape-to-close, ::backdrop, top-layer rendering. Unlike Drawer, needs almost no positioning CSS at all — showModal()'s own UA stylesheet already centers a <dialog> via position:fixed + inset:0 + margin:auto, so this component only sets width/radius/shadow/padding on top of that native default. radius.xl specifically — already named for this exact case in radius's own legend ('Prominent surfaces: modals, large panels, hero cards'), not a new choice. Kept as a token file separate from Drawer per the same prior explicit decision (both are '<dialog> with showModal()' underneath, but centered-floating vs. edge-attached differ enough in sizing/radius/positioning to earn separate files). Nested modals (a modal opened from within another modal) 'just work' via the browser's own native top-layer stacking order — no z-index needed, unlike the manual modal-2/modal-overlay-2 tiers z-index.tokens.json defines for a non-native implementation. Single fixed width (dim.96, 384px) — no size grid, same reasoning as Drawer's single width; revisit only if a real need for a size variant appears. Header and footer are both optional composition, same as Card/Drawer — a Modal can be body-only. The close button and footer actions are real interactive elements with their own hover/active/focus states (the same fill.neutral/fill.neutralHover/fill.neutralActive/fill.primary or fill.danger recipe Button itself uses), not unstyled placeholders.

gap.$description: 12px — internal flex gap within the header row (title-to-close-button) and footer row (button-to-button), same reasoning as Drawer's own gap after the divider-width fix: section-to-section spacing comes from each section's own full padding, so the divider spans the whole modal width instead of sitting inset.

transitionDuration.$description: Literal, not a token, same precedent as Drawer/Tooltip. Slightly quicker than Drawer's 250ms — a centered scale/fade reads fine faster than an edge slide covering more distance.

alert.$description: AlertDialog (Radix's term) — a behavioral variant, not a visual one: identical bg/radius/shadow/padding to plain Modal, zero new tokens. The difference is what the JS does, not what anything looks like. For a genuinely critical confirmation (irreversible delete, destructive action) the dismiss-on-outside-click and Escape-to-close both get disabled, and there's no header close (×) — the only way out is clicking one of the footer actions. Reuses Modal's own showModal()/native-<dialog> mechanism; the click-outside script skips any dialog carrying the alert marker, and Escape is blocked by preventDefault()-ing the dialog's native 'cancel' event. Use sparingly — most confirmations don't need to be this strict; a plain Modal with Cancel/Delete already covers the common case.
